summary: A capacity violation ends a restyled slide without a repair call only when it is about an element that owns source text; the model's own decoration is something a repair call can fix.
invariants: An ordinary authored deck, which owns all of its text, keeps the original classification unchanged.
A violation that names an element owning source text, or that carries a measurement instead of an element, stays terminal.
Source ownership is read from the slide's own HTML: an element carrying data-source-block-id, or a deterministic source QID.
Safety issues are still reported; only the code changes, and the caller already lets a safety classification continue into repair.
forbidden: End a deck without a repair call because the model's own ornament failed a capacity check.
Relax the classification for elements that render immutable source text.
rationale: Operation 3d0b9e72 authored 35 of 35 slides and was ended by slide 16's hero mark: a '+' ornament the browser could not see, clipped, and overlapping the source block beside it. The preflight classified it authored_slide_capacity_exceeded and raised before any repair call.
Capacity is terminal because verbatim source text cannot be shortened to fit. An ornament is not source text: shrinking, moving or dropping it is exactly what a repair call does.
Replayed on the stored artifact of that slide the classification moves from authored_slide_capacity_exceeded to authored_composition_safety_gate_failed, which the caller allows into repair.
